source.title: Holiday calendars written for Prospero Companion
source.note: Public holidays and observances from general knowledge. Moved weekend dates ("observed" days) and religious holidays on lunar calendars are not included.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: A slow day after the night before; most things closed.

holidays.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
holidays.summary: Federal holiday with days of service and marches; schools and government offices close.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.summary: Restaurants book up; cards and flowers.

holidays.name: Presidents' Day
holidays.summary: Federal holiday; government offices and many schools close, and stores run sales.

holidays.name: St. Patrick's Day
holidays.summary: Green beer, parades and crowded pubs.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church services, egg hunts and family brunch.

holidays.name: Mother's Day
holidays.summary: Brunch reservations and calls home.

holidays.name: Memorial Day
holidays.summary: The unofficial start of summer: cookouts, beaches and remembrance of the war dead.

holidays.name: Father's Day
holidays.summary: Cookouts and calls home.

holidays.name: Juneteenth
holidays.summary: Marks the end of slavery in the United States; festivals and cookouts.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.summary: Fireworks, cookouts and a day off.

holidays.name: Labor Day
holidays.summary: The unofficial end of summer and a long weekend.

holidays.name: Halloween
holidays.summary: Costumes, trick-or-treating and parties.

holidays.name: Veterans Day
holidays.summary: Federal holiday; government offices and banks close.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving
holidays.summary: A big family meal, football and travel; most things close.

holidays.name: Christmas Eve
holidays.summary: Last-minute shopping and family gatherings; many offices close early.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Presents and family; almost everything closes.

holidays.name: New Year's Eve
holidays.summary: Parties and countdowns at midnight.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Calls on friends and an open house in the parlour.

holidays.name: Washington's Birthday
holidays.summary: Speeches, a ball and a day off for banks and offices.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church in new clothes and a big dinner after.

holidays.name: Decoration Day
holidays.summary: Veterans and townsfolk decorate soldiers' graves with flowers, with a procession and speeches.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.summary: The biggest day of the year: parade, oration, races, a barbecue and fireworks.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving Day
holidays.summary: Proclaimed each year for the last Thursday of November: church, turkey and a shooting match.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Church, a tree, presents and a big dinner.

holidays.name: New Year's Day
holidays.summary: Not a holiday in England; Scots keep Hogmanay.

holidays.name: Lady Day
holidays.summary: A quarter day: rents fall due and servants' terms change.

holidays.name: Shrove Tuesday
holidays.summary: Pancake day, with football in some towns.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.summary: Shops shut, hot cross buns and church.

holidays.name: Easter Sunday
holidays.summary: Church and a family dinner.

holidays.name: Easter Monday
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: excursion trains, fairs and Hampstead Heath crowded with day-trippers.

holidays.name: The Queen's Birthday
holidays.summary: Flags, a royal salute and, in the colonies, a holiday.

holidays.name: Whit Monday
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: Whit walks, Sunday-school treats and excursions.

holidays.name: Midsummer Day
holidays.summary: A quarter day when rents fall due.

holidays.name: August Bank Holiday
holidays.summary: The first Monday in August: seaside trips, crowded trains and fairs.

holidays.name: Michaelmas
holidays.summary: A quarter day; goose for dinner and hiring fairs.

holidays.name: Guy Fawkes Night
holidays.summary: Bonfires, guys carried through the streets and fireworks.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Church, a goose or a joint, plum pudding and family.

holidays.name: Boxing Day
holidays.summary: A bank holiday: Christmas boxes for tradesmen and servants, and the pantomime season opens.

holidays.name: Twelfth Night
holidays.summary: The last night of Christmas: a bean in the cake makes a king for the evening.

holidays.name: Epiphany
holidays.summary: The end of the twelve days of Christmas.

holidays.name: Plough Monday
holidays.summary: Ploughboys drag a decorated plough round the town begging for pennies before work starts again.

holidays.name: Candlemas
holidays.summary: Candles blessed in church and carried in procession.

holidays.name: Shrove Tuesday
holidays.summary: Feasting, cock-throwing and football before Lent.

holidays.name: Ash Wednesday
holidays.summary: Lent begins: no meat until Easter.

holidays.name: Lady Day
holidays.summary: The Annunciation and the start of the year; a quarter day.

holidays.name: Palm Sunday
holidays.summary: Procession with yew and willow for palms.

holidays.name: Good Friday
holidays.summary: Creeping to the cross; a day of fasting.

holidays.name: Easter Day
holidays.summary: Lent ends: meat, eggs and ale, and a day free of work.

holidays.name: Hock Monday
holidays.summary: The women of the town rope the men and let them go for a forfeit; the men return the favour next day.

holidays.name: May Day
holidays.summary: Bringing in the may at dawn, a maypole and dancing.

holidays.name: Ascension Day
holidays.summary: Beating the bounds of the parish.

holidays.name: Whitsunday (Pentecost)
holidays.summary: A great feast; the king holds court and church ales are brewed.

holidays.name: St John's Eve
holidays.summary: Bonfires on the hills and watch fires in the town.

holidays.name: Lammas
holidays.summary: Loaf-mass: bread from the first wheat blessed in church.

holidays.name: Michaelmas
holidays.summary: Rents and reeves' accounts due, and a goose for dinner.

holidays.name: All Hallows
holidays.summary: Bells rung for the dead through the night before.

holidays.name: Martinmas
holidays.summary: Beasts slaughtered and salted for winter; a feast of fresh meat.

holidays.name: Christmas Day
holidays.summary: Twelve days of feasting, games and no work in the fields.
